why:
I checked both must_not items against the two briefs.

Item 1: Check 3 builds the list from the module's actual exports and compares it with the README headings. A README that has padLeft but no slugify gives "missing: slugify". The brief also says outright: "if it is still missing, this check FAILS." So this item is not broken.

Item 2: Check 1's values ('00042', '   42', '**ab', 'xxx') all follow from line 1, and nothing tests a multi-character fill or limits fill to one character. Check 2 only asks that s comes back unchanged. Check 3 accepts a heading at any level that names the function, so it doesn't force a layout. "With section text below it" is a reasonable reading of "section". Check 4 asks for exit code 0 and zero failures. The parameter count isn't checked, and the multi-character fill note is advisory only. The builder's `## name(...)` instruction isn't a PASS/FAIL condition, so I didn't count it.

One weak spot, which I judged minor: Check 4 looks for the literal "# fail 0", which some test output formats don't print even when all tests pass.
